Mental Health Care Plan Details
(Address each principal problem identified in Clinical Assessment - Section A. Add additional problems as relevant.)

Principal Problem:
- Situational work-related stress (patient reports manageable “good stress” without mood disturbance)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Maintain functioning at work while recovering from illness
  - Monitor stress levels and mood; seek help if stress becomes unmanageable
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Screen for emerging anxiety/depressive symptoms if stress or physical symptoms persist
  - Provide brief advice on stress management and supports
- Actions (Patient):
  - Monitor mood, sleep, appetite, and energy over the next 2–4 weeks
  - Return promptly if experiencing persistent low mood, anhedonia, excessive worry, sleep disturbance, or functional decline
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Offer mental health review if patient reports worsening stress or mood
  - Provide information on stress management resources and when to seek care
  - Consider formal screening (e.g., PHQ-9/GAD-7) at follow-up if concerns arise

Secondary Problem (if applicable):
- Acute viral upper respiratory tract illness affecting energy and function
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Rest and recover; return to baseline activity
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Symptomatic management; reassess if not improving
- Actions (Patient):
  - Rest, maintain hydration, continue over-the-counter analgesics as advised; seek care earlier for high fever, increased breathlessness, or chest pain
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Safety-net advice provided; arrange follow-up if symptoms persist beyond one week or worsen
